# External documentation manifest

Third-party documentation gathered while planning, so a plan's claims about an external
library, API or service can be checked rather than trusted.

The agent modes treat an unknown third-party interface as a blocking condition: rather
than guessing at a method signature, the architect fetches the real documentation with
the Oxylabs MCP server, records it here, and cites it in the plan.

## Format

**One line per entry**, in the table below:

```text
| URL | Title | Description |
```

* **URL** — the canonical source, linked so a reader can open it.
* **Title** — the page's own title, not a paraphrase.
* **Description** — one sentence on what the page covers. One sentence, not a summary.

## What gets saved in full, and what does not

| Case | Action |
| --- | --- |
| The page answers the question being planned | Save it in full at `doc/external/<vendor>/<page-slug>.md`, link it from the entry below |
| The page is adjacent, but not needed right now | Record the link and the one-sentence description only |

`<vendor>` is the owner of the documentation, lowercase (`oxylabs`, `stripe`, `vllm`).
`<page-slug>` is a kebab-case slug derived from the page title. One page per file, with
the source URL recorded at the top of the file, so an entry can cite a single path.

Saving a vendor's whole site is not the goal: it buries the page that mattered and makes
the diff unreviewable. Saving a fragment is not either, because the next reader re-fetches
it. Save what answers the question, in full.

## Why this is committed

The research is a team asset and is reviewable in the pull request that relies on it. A
gitignored cache would be re-scraped by every developer and would silently rot.

Two rules follow from that:

* Update this manifest in the same change that saves a page — a saved page absent from
  the manifest is unfindable.
* Never commit credentials, tokens or private endpoints into `doc/external/`.

| [https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/managing-your-personal-access-tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/managing-your-personal-access-tokens) | Managing your personal access tokens — GitHub Docs | The permission table behind the blocked `setup-repo` gate's printed token recipe and the token-scope probes: the pre-fill parameter names (`target_name`, one `<permission>` parameter per grant, `write` implying `read`), the `workflows` row with **no `read` level**, `metadata` read-only and implicit, the Checks-API restriction and the "read-only access to all public repositories" caveat on every fine-grained token, and the classic-token grant that reaches every repository the owner can see — saved in full at [`doc/external/github/fine-grained-personal-access-tokens.md`](github/fine-grained-personal-access-tokens.md). |
| [https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/issues](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/issues) | REST API endpoints for issues — GitHub Docs | The intake loop's issue read: `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}` on **Issues: read** returns `number`, `title` and `body` — `body` being the untrusted text that must reach the model quoted — and answers `301` for a transferred issue, `410` for a deleted-but-readable one and `404` for an unreadable one — saved in full at [`doc/external/github/rest-api-endpoints-for-issues.md`](github/rest-api-endpoints-for-issues.md). |
| [https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/comments](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/comments) | REST API endpoints for issue comments — GitHub Docs | How progress is posted: `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/comments` takes exactly one required body parameter, `body`, succeeds with **`201` not `200`**, and carries GitHub's own secondary-rate-limit warning — which is why progress comments stay few and short — saved in full at [`doc/external/github/rest-api-endpoints-for-issue-comments.md`](github/rest-api-endpoints-for-issue-comments.md). |
| [https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/pulls](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/pulls) | REST API endpoints for pull requests — GitHub Docs | How delivery happens: `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls` requires `head` and `base` (plus `title` unless `issue` is given), takes the description as a plain `body` string, succeeds with **`201`**, rejects a duplicate or unpushed head with `422`, and returns `number`, `html_url` and `head.sha` — the SHA the CI lookup keys on — saved in full at [`doc/external/github/rest-api-endpoints-for-pull-requests.md`](github/rest-api-endpoints-for-pull-requests.md). |
| [https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-runs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-runs) | REST API endpoints for workflow runs — GitHub Docs | How the run reads its own CI on **Actions: read**: `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs?head_sha=…` returns an **envelope** `{"total_count", "workflow_runs"}` rather than a bare array, `conclusion` is `null` until `status` is `completed`, no runs is `200` with an empty array rather than `404`, and every re-run/cancel/delete endpoint needs Actions **write** — which the repo-scoped token withholds — saved in full at [`doc/external/github/rest-api-endpoints-for-workflow-runs.md`](github/rest-api-endpoints-for-workflow-runs.md). |
| [https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/managing-your-personal-access-tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/managing-your-personal-access-tokens) | Managing your personal access tokens — GitHub Docs | Why the loop's token is a fine-grained PAT limited to one repository: `administration` and `workflows` are separate permissions that can simply be withheld, every fine-grained token keeps read-only access to all public repos, and a fine-grained token cannot call the Checks API — so the CI outcome is read through Actions workflow runs, not check runs — saved in full at [`doc/external/github/fine-grained-personal-access-tokens.md`](github/fine-grained-personal-access-tokens.md). |
